review_comments.body:
duplicate method definition - `downsize` is defined twice with different signatures (lines 145-147 and 149-151). The second definition will override the first, making the `max_width, max_height` signature inaccessible.

```suggestion
  def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions_or_width, height_or_opts=nil, opts={})
    if height_or_opts.is_a?(Hash)
      # Called with dimensions string: downsize(from, to, "80%", opts)
      optimize("downsize", from, to, dimensions_or_width, height_or_opts)
    else
      # Called with width/height: downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)
      optimize("downsize", from, to, "#{dimensions_or_width}x#{height_or_opts}", opts)
    end
  end
```

this loop may not terminate if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails to reduce file size (e.g., already heavily compressed images, certain formats). After 5 attempts with no size reduction, you'll still have an oversized file. Add a check to break if file size doesn't decrease between iterations.

```suggestion
      # allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size
      if tempfile && tempfile.size > 0 && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)
        attempt = 5
        previous_size = tempfile.size
        while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes
          OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)
          attempt -= 1
          # Break if file size didn't change (can't compress further)
          break if tempfile.size >= previous_size
          previous_size = tempfile.size
        end
      end
```

hardcoded 10MB limit replaces dynamic `SiteSettings` lookup, creating inconsistency between client validation and server-side processing. Users may upload files that pass client validation but fail server validation if `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` differs from 10MB.
hardcoded 10MB limit in error message creates inconsistency with actual validation - error message will always show 10MB even if the setting is different.

review_comments.body: This method has a race condition - if two requests check the same email simultaneously, both will increment `match_count` independently, potentially causing incorrect counts. Additionally, the method modifies database state during what appears to be a read operation (validation), which violates separation of concerns and could cause unexpected side effects. Consider separating the "check if blocked" logic from the "track statistics" logic.

`and` keyword has lower precedence than `&&`. This line will be evaluated as `(record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value))` but if any developer adds additional conditions later, it could cause precedence bugs.

    if record.errors[attribute].blank? && BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)

Origin validation is backwards - `indexOf` returns position or -1. This checks if `discourseUrl` contains the origin, not if origin starts with `discourseUrl`. Attacker at `evil.comdiscourseUrl.com` would pass.
